thread:
incbot: INCIDENT ALERT — multiple BGP withdraws observed from upstream provider TransitVia affecting eu-central AZ-C and AZ-D egress. Packet loss and high latency to public prefixes reported. Pager: oncall-alex.

oncall-alex: acked, I'm on it. Initial question — is this hitting customer traffic or internal health checks?

netops-jordan: seeing BGP session resets from TransitVia on both peering sessions in AZ-C and AZ-D around 22:00 UTC. Repeated withdraws for several /24s. quick scrub from our edge: 
```
# show bgp summary vrf BLUE | include TransitVia
TransitVia-AS  192.0.2.10    ESTAB  4 prefixes  650  flaps=12
TransitVia-AS  198.51.100.10  ESTAB  0 prefixes  650  flaps=9
```
withdraw timestamps match our loss window.

eng-ryan: apps show elevated 5xx for eu-central (api latency 300-800ms, error rate spike at 22:05 UTC). Canary traffic routed through AZ-C, so yes customer impact. Some customers reported API timeouts.

support-sam: several customer tickets escalated — lots of timeouts and slow responses from eu instances. CS is triaging. cc @customer-success-liz

customer-success-liz: we're seeing increased contact from a couple enterprise customers in EU, asking if this is on our side. They saw traffic blackholes to certain IP ranges.

netops-jordan: grabbing traceroutes — sample to 203.0.113.45 (affected prefix):
```
traceroute to 203.0.113.45 (22:10 UTC)
 1  10.0.0.1  0.6 ms
 2  192.0.2.1  1.2 ms
 3  198.51.100.1  200 ms  *  *
 4  * * *
```
shows egress blackhole after our peering.

oncall-alex: can we fail traffic over to CarrierB (backup transit) for eu-central until TransitVia stabilizes? What are risk/steps?

netops-jordan: We have pre-provisioned BGP communities that prefer CarrierB at the route-map level. Plan: 1) announce customer prefixes to CarrierB with higher localpref via community 65000:200 2) temporarily de-preference TransitVia by prepending to their sessions. This will shift traffic within ~120s for most flows.

eng-ryan: if we move heavy egress to CarrierB, we should watch latency for in-region traffic — some customers prefer TransitVia path. But availability is higher priority now.

sre-maya: I'm going to take lead on mitigation. I'll coordinate config changes and monitor health checks. Handoff: oncall-alex handing to sre-maya.

oncall-alex: handing off to @sre-maya — you have the pager.

sre-maya: executing planned mitigation now. Snippet of commands I'll run on edge-bgp01/eu-c: 
```
# route-map PREFER-CARRIER permit 10
 set community 65000:200 additive
 set local-preference 200

# apply to export towards CarrierB
```
Applying to both AZ-C and AZ-D edges.

netops-jordan: also adding one-shot prepends to TransitVia sessions to make them less preferred until they stop flapping: 
```
neighbor 192.0.2.10 route-map PREPEND-TO-TransitVia out
route-map PREPEND-TO-TransitVia permit 10
 set as-path prepend 65001 65001 65001
```

sre-maya: change applied on eu-c edges at 22:14 UTC. Monitoring BGP table and traffic.

transit-team@provider: FYI — we are currently investigating a flapping aggregation link in our eu-core POP causing session resets for customers on link-group A. We're rolling a fix now. ETA 30-60m.

netops-jordan: after change, BGP table shows majority of affected prefixes now preferred via CarrierB. Latency for some customers increased ~40ms but packetloss dropped to near 0.

eng-ryan: app metrics improving — 5xx rate trending down, tail p95 latency back to acceptable.

support-sam: telling affected customers we've applied a failover to backup transit to restore connectivity; we'll follow up with root cause once TransitVia confirms.

oncall-alex: tagging incident status: partial mitigation achieved via reroute to CarrierB. Still monitoring for residual flaps and route convergence.

transit-team@provider: we've applied a hardware swap on the flapping link, BGP session stability improving on our side. Please confirm if you see stable sessions for the previously affected feeds.

netops-jordan: yes — sessions to TransitVia show 0 flaps in the last 10m. Traffic has mostly normalized. We'll keep the prepends/communities in place for a cool-down period (30m) then gradually remove.

sre-maya: rolling back prepends and communities at 22:47 UTC in a controlled manner. Removing from AZ-D first, AZ-C next.

eng-ryan: everything looks steady. No new error surges in EU.

support-sam: notifying customers: issue mitigated via reroute; investigating root cause with TransitVia.

oncall-alex: incident status -> mitigated. On-call handback to main rotation. scheduling post-incident review tomorrow 09:30 UTC.

transit-team@provider: thanks for quick coordination. We'll follow up with detailed RCA on our maintenance-induced flap.

incbot: INCIDENT RESOLVED — mitigation confirmed and traffic normalized. Please file a postmortem and tag with #networking #upstream #euc.

customer-success-liz: adding notes for impacted customers and follow-up comms.

sre-maya: creating the doc now and will include timeline, config changes, and next steps: - ask TransitVia for maintenance window guarantees - expand BGP healthchecks and automated failover playbook - simulation to validate cross-region failover latency impact.

oncall-alex: thanks everyone. Closing thread after PM/RCA posted. :white_check_mark:
